Male Urinogenital Duct (Urine + Sperm) vs Female Ureter (Urine Only)
quickSummary: The excretory system comprises paired mesonephric kidneys, ureters, a ventral bilobed urinary bladder, and cloaca. Adult frogs are Ureotelic (urea synthesized in liver), whereas aquatic tadpoles are Ammonotelic (ammonia). In males, the ureter functions as a Urinogenital Duct carrying both urine and spermatozoa; in females, ureters carry only urine.

conceptBreakdown.content:
The excretory apparatus eliminates nitrogenous wastes and maintains osmotic fluid balance.

### Kidney Microanatomy
• **Mesonephric Kidneys**: Pair of dark red, elongated, bean-shaped structures on either side of the vertebral column.
• **Adrenal Gland**: A bright yellow, narrow endocrine strip located on the ventral surface of each kidney.
• **Nephrons (Uriniferous Tubules)**: $\approx 2,000$ structural units per kidney, each starting with a **Bowman's Capsule** enclosing a **Glomerulus** (Malpighian Body).

conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Ureotelism & Sex Differences in Ureters
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
NITROGENOUS EXCRETION MODES
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  TADPOLE LARVA (Aquatic)                                 ADULT FROG (Terrestrial)
 ├── Excretes AMMONIA (Ammonotelic)                      ├── Excretes UREA (Ureotelic)
 └── Flushed by abundant water                           └── Synthesized in Liver via Urea Cycle
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Metabolic Shift**: Tadpoles are **Ammonotelic**; adult frogs are **Ureotelic** (ammonia synthesized into urea in the liver via the Krebs-Henseleit cycle).
• **Ureter Dimorphism**:
  - **In Males**: Ureters act as **Urinogenital Ducts** carrying both urine from kidneys and sperm from Bidder's canal into the cloaca.
  - **In Females**: Ureters carry **only urine** and open separately from oviducts into the cloaca.
• **Urinary Bladder**: A large, thin-walled, bilobed distensible sac located ventral to the rectum, opening into the ventral cloacal wall.
